key: Google Maps vs. the village directions
name: ch02_maps_destination_search
alt: A traveller types only a destination into a phone map, and the app picks the route over a brand-new flyover without the request changing.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of the outskirts of a growing Indian town at late morning. In the left foreground, a young woman in a kurta and jeans with a sling bag stands beside her parked scooter, holding up a large smartphone toward the viewer. The phone screen is drawn big and clear: a search box at the top with a single destination pin icon and a house with a blue gate, and below it a simple map where a bright highlighted route line has been drawn automatically. She has typed only where she wants to go, nothing about how. In the middle of the scene, the real roads mirror the phone map: an old winding lane goes the long way round past a temple and a market, while a brand-new concrete flyover, still with a festive ribbon and a few marigold garlands on its railing from its opening day, cuts straight across a railway line. The highlighted route on the phone matches the flyover, and a dotted arrow links the screen to the flyover. On the far right, in the distance, the house with the blue gate waits at the end of the route. A small inset bubble near the phone shows the same typed request card twice, unchanged, once with the old lane and once with the new flyover, to show the request never had to be rewritten. Bright clear daylight, relaxed and modern mood. Labels: "WHAT" above the search box on the phone, "HOW" along the highlighted route over the flyover.

key: CODASYL is the village directions again
name: ch02_codasyl_vs_address_search
alt: Split picture: on the left a man follows one fixed chain of directions house by house; on the right a woman uses a map search box to jump straight to any house or to every house with a blue gate.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same small village street seen from above, with a row of five small houses of different colours, two of them with bright blue gates, and lanes linking them. LEFT panel: an older postman in a khaki uniform with a cloth bag walks a single chain of footprints that starts at a bus stand and must pass every house in order, one after another; arrows link house to house in one fixed sequence, and he cannot reach the fourth house without first passing the first three. A road-works barrier blocks one lane on his chain, and he stands scratching his head at it with a crumpled list of directions, a question mark above him. RIGHT panel: the same village street, but a young delivery woman in a cap holds a tablet showing a map with a search box; from the search box two kinds of jumps fly straight down to the houses: one bold arrow lands directly on a single house by its house number badge, and a fan of thinner arrows lands on both houses with blue gates at once, as if she had searched for every blue gate. Extra lanes on the right side connect houses freely in any direction, not only in a line. Clean midday light, calm and orderly. Labels: "FOLLOW THE ROUTE" above the left panel, "JUMP BY ADDRESS" above the right panel.

key: The dream of one national register
name: ch02_national_register_dream
alt: A dream bubble shows a shop, a school and a hospital feeding one shared register that a computer reads, while on the ground their owners argue over different paper forms.
scene: A two-level picture, a dream above and reality below. TOP half: a large soft cloud-shaped dream bubble drawn above a town. Inside it, a small hospital with a red cross, a school with a bell tower, and a kirana shop each send a neat identical card along straight glowing lines into one big central register book, and a friendly desktop computer beside the book answers a question drawn as an inset: a hospital bed icon with a green tick and an insurance card icon with a green tick, meaning a free ICU bed that accepts your card. Everything in the dream is perfectly lined up and matching. BOTTOM half: the real town square at ground level, with the same three buildings. In front of them stand the hospital administrator in a white coat, the school headmistress in a sari holding a register, and the shopkeeper in a vest holding a notebook, each clutching a differently shaped form of their own, one square, one long, one folded, and gesturing at each other in a friendly but stubborn disagreement. A tiny snail crawls slowly along a long road sign beside them to show slow progress. In the bottom-right corner, a single office building with its own small neat stack of matching cards shows that the shared format still works inside one company. Bright daylight below, dreamy pastel glow above. Labels: "THE DREAM" inside the top of the bubble, "REALITY" at the bottom left of the ground scene.

name: ch02_worksheet_blanks_query
alt: A student tries many name cards in the blank of a worksheet and keeps every card that makes all the lines true at once.
scene: An Indian classroom desk seen from slightly above, with a large printed worksheet lying on it. The worksheet has three short lines stacked one under another, drawn with pictures rather than words: in the first line, a blank box followed by a small baby-cradle icon and an arrow to a town pin; in the second line, the town pin followed by a nested-boxes icon and an arrow to a larger state shape; in the third line, the state shape followed by the same nested-boxes icon and an arrow to a big country outline. The blank box in the first line has a dotted border. A curious schoolgirl in a uniform with two plaits sits at the desk holding a stack of small name cards, each with a different person's face, and slides them one at a time into the blank. To the right of the worksheet, cards that made all three lines true are clipped together in a neat bundle with green ticks, several of them, not just one. To the left, cards that failed one of the lines lie in a small discard pile with little red crosses. A teacher in a sari leans over her shoulder smiling, pointing at the bundle to show that every fitting card counts as an answer. Warm morning light through a window, focused and calm. Labels: "?PERSON" inside the blank box, "EVERY FIT" above the bundle of ticked cards.
